column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew addresses the valuation as “your valuation”; BSB says “the value of persons.”
The Hebrew repeats “your valuation” and uses the age expressions “a son of twenty years” and “a son of sixty years”; BSB uses “the valuation” first and gives the ages without the son image.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the age expressions “a son of five years” and “a son of twenty years”; BSB gives the ages directly.
The Hebrew uses “a son of a month” and “a son of five years” for the ages and repeats “your valuation” for the female; BSB gives the ages directly and states the valuation once.
The Hebrew uses “a son of sixty years and upward”; BSB gives the age as “sixty years of age or older.”
The Hebrew describes affordability as what the vower’s “hand can reach” and names “the priest” three times; BSB says “can afford” and names the priest once.
The Hebrew begins “if an animal,” without an explicit vowing verb here; BSB supplies “If he vows an animal.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses active plural “they shall not present” and active singular “he shall present”; BSB uses passive “may not be brought” and “must be presented.”
The Hebrew says “between good and bad” and addresses “your valuation, priest”; BSB says “whether high or low” and refers to the priest in the third person.
The Hebrew does not explicitly identify an “owner” or add a decision verb; BSB says “the owner decides to redeem.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the idiom “according to the mouth of its seed”; BSB explains the valuation as proportional to “the seed required for it.”
The Hebrew says “from the year of Jubilee”; BSB says “during the Year of Jubilee.”
The Hebrew says a deduction will be made “from your valuation”; BSB makes the valuation the subject that “will be reduced.”
The Hebrew emphasizes redeeming by repeating the verb; BSB instead adds “decides to redeem.”
The Hebrew joins the two conditions with “and if”; BSB uses “or if.”
The Hebrew says the field will belong to singular “the priest”; BSB uses plural “the priests.”

The Hebrew uses a birth verb in “a firstborn which is born first to the LORD”; BSB explains the restriction with “because a firstborn belongs to the LORD.”

The Hebrew calls devoted property “holiness of holinesses”; BSB says “most holy.”
